display: Nurse in Kuala Lumpur; my family has worked the Selayang wholesale market for three generations.

signals.text: I work nights on a medical ward and I'm very tired. I need real leave, but I can't see who would cover my shifts.
My son is fifteen, wants to study engineering in Taiwan, and we will start looking at school lists and scholarships next month.
I want to hear from someone who has been through the Taiwan university route as a Malaysian student or parent: fees, scholarships, dorms, and when to start.
I'm thinking about visiting Taipei in March and bringing my son to see campuses.
My mother is seventy and has type 2 diabetes. I'd like practical ways to help her eat well without making her give up kuih completely.
A cousin of mine runs a fruit-import stall at Selayang market. Chinese navel oranges reach him through two middlemen, so his margin is nearly gone.
The temple food bank I volunteer at now serves about forty families a week, up from thirty-five, and the families have asked for fresh vegetables.
My son is good at maths and asks questions I can't answer. I'd welcome a patient maths or engineering mentor for a quiet fifteen-year-old.
I bake kaya puffs and pineapple tarts from my grandmother's recipe, but my small home oven runs hot and I'm not sure how to adjust.
I'm saving every month for my son's overseas university costs and I know it isn't enough yet. I'm looking for scholarships or cheaper routes.
Some of the elderly patients I look after can't read messages from family abroad because of poor eyesight or language, and that matters a lot to them.

offers.text: I'm a registered nurse with twelve years on medical and surgical wards. I can explain hospital care, diabetes basics and care routines in plain language.
I speak English, Malay, Cantonese and Mandarin, and I read both simplified and traditional Chinese. I can help with reading or translating letters and messages, and with talking to older relatives.
Through uncles and cousins I know people in the Selayang wholesale market: vegetables, fruit and durian traders.
I know the Malaysian public hospital system from the inside, including how to navigate clinics, appointments and long-term care for elderly relatives.
I have my grandmother's kaya puff and pineapple tart recipes and can bake in small batches.
I volunteer on Sunday mornings at a temple food bank and can help connect food donors or suppliers to it.
I have experience teaching nursing and explaining health topics to learners and families.
I can introduce a trusted trader to my uncle or cousins at Selayang. The introduction is only a first step, and any deal is theirs to decide.

catchers.hypo: I run an orchard or packing house in China that exports Chinese navel oranges. I'm looking for a reliable small importer in Kuala Lumpur and don't want to sell through layers of agents.
catchers.can: I can introduce my cousin, who runs a fruit-import stall at Selayang market and currently buys through two middlemen. I would only make the introduction, and they would negotiate directly.
catchers.confirm: Can you ship directly to Port Klang, with fixed per-carton quotes and a willingness to work with a small stall rather than a large chain?

catchers.hypo: I'm a Malaysian student or parent who went through the Taiwan university application route. I'm happy to share what worked on fees, scholarships and dormitories.
catchers.can: I'd gladly listen and ask questions for my son, who is fifteen and wants to study engineering in Taiwan, and I could share back what I learn with other parents.
catchers.confirm: Did you apply to Taiwanese universities from Malaysia yourself, or help your own child do it, within the last five years?

catchers.hypo: I run a small charity or food-aid programme and have surplus vegetables, rice or cooking oil. I want to give it to families who really need it.
catchers.can: I can connect you to my temple food bank, which serves about forty families a week and has asked for vegetables. I can also ask my uncle at the market about supply.
catchers.confirm: Is the donation regular or one-off, and can it be delivered to Selayang or Kuala Lumpur on a weekday?

catchers.hypo: My elderly parent in Malaysia has type 2 diabetes and I live abroad. I don't know how to help with their appointments and diet from far away.
catchers.can: I can share my approach to a food diary, check-up routines and talking to the clinic. I've been doing this for my own mother for years. I can't give medical advice for a particular person.
catchers.confirm: Are you looking for practical routines and caregiver experience, and not for a diagnosis or prescription?

catchers.hypo: My grandmother in Kuala Lumpur only reads Chinese and her eyesight is failing. I'm abroad and want someone to help her read and answer family messages.
catchers.can: I can help with reading and replying in Cantonese or Mandarin, simplified or traditional, or point to someone nearby who can.
catchers.confirm: Does the person need help in Cantonese, Mandarin or both, and is it occasional help with messages and not daily care?

catchers.hypo: I teach engineering or maths and want to mentor a bright teenager who is thinking of studying in Taiwan.
catchers.can: My son Jun Wei is fifteen, quiet and good at maths, and wants to study engineering. I would pass on your message and arrange a short call with his involvement.
catchers.confirm: Are you offering mentoring for a teenager that is free or low cost and comfortable for a shy student, and not a paid tutoring centre?

catchers.hypo: I'm a nurse in Malaysia who is exhausted from night shifts. I'm looking for another nurse to swap or cover shifts so I can take leave.
catchers.can: I'm in the same situation and can talk through how colleagues cover shifts and handle burnout. I can't change hospital rosters.
catchers.confirm: Are you looking for a peer to talk with, and not a formal staffing agency or replacement hire?

catchers.hypo: I'm a home baker who wants to swap recipes and tips on small ovens, or I'd like to buy traditional Malaysian Chinese pastries for an event.
catchers.can: I can swap tips on kaya puffs and pineapple tarts and talk about oven temperature problems. I bake small batches and give most of them away, so I'm not set up for larger orders.
catchers.confirm: Is this a recipe or tips exchange, or a small event order of a few dozen pieces?

forbids.text: I will never share patient information from my work.
I can't take more than two days of leave at a time.
I work nights, so mornings are for sleep and I can't take calls or meetings then.
I won't use my son's tuition savings for anything else.
I don't push business at family gatherings, and I only make introductions when both sides want them.
I'm not a doctor and can't diagnose, prescribe or give medical advice for a particular person.
I won't invest or put in my own money into other people's ventures.

projects.name: Son's Taiwan university plan
projects.text: Planning an engineering degree in Taiwan for my fifteen-year-old son: school lists, scholarships, costs, dormitory and a possible March campus visit.
roles_needed: Malaysian student or parent with Taiwan university experience
engineering or maths mentor for a teenager

projects.name: Temple food bank fresh vegetable supply
projects.text: Families at the Sunday temple food bank have asked for vegetables. We serve about forty families a week and need a steady, low-cost supply.

policy.t1: When there is a real sign of a fit, I'm willing to share my cousin's fruit-stall situation (supply chain and margin concerns), my son's Taiwan study plan and my mother's diabetes care routine.
policy.t2: When a fit is likely and I know who you are, I'm willing to share family tensions and details of my savings plan for my son.
policy.never: I never share hospital patient information or anything about my husband's departure.
